title: Two kinds of values: text and numbers
idea: A value is either TEXT (a string, in quotes) or a NUMBER (no quotes). The computer keeps them apart.

exercises.prompt: Python values come in kinds (called 'types'). Which two kinds have we been using?
exercises.explanation: Everything so far has been either text (a string, inside quotes) or a number. The computer treats them differently.

exercises.prompt: Which of these is TEXT (a string)?
exercises.explanation: The quotes are the giveaway. "hello" is text. The others are numbers.

exercises.prompt: Which of these is a NUMBER?
exercises.explanation: 25 with no quotes is a number. "25" with quotes is text that happens to look like a number.

exercises.prompt: "7" (with quotes) and 7 (no quotes) are the same kind of value.
exercises.explanation: They look alike but are different kinds. "7" is text; 7 is a number. This difference causes a famous bug — you'll meet it soon.

exercises.prompt: Select EVERY value here that is text (a string).
exercises.explanation: Text is whatever sits inside quotes: "dog" and "5". The bare 9 and 12 are numbers.

exercises.prompt: Match each value to its kind.
exercises.explanation: Quotes decide it. "100" is text even though it looks like a number; 100 alone is a real number.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

age = 12
print(age)
exercises.explanation: age holds the number 12. Printing it shows 12 — the quotes you see in text never appear for a number.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

name = "12"
print(name)
exercises.explanation: The screen shows 12 either way! You can't SEE the quotes in the output — but inside, name is text, not a number.

exercises.prompt: You can tell a value's kind by whether it is written inside quotes.
exercises.explanation: Quotes mean text. No quotes (just digits) means a number. That one habit saves you from many bugs.

exercises.prompt: Why does it matter whether a value is text or a number?
options: The computer does different things to each — math on numbers, joining on text
Numbers cannot be stored in variables
exercises.explanation: Knowing the kind tells you what the computer will DO. Next lesson: how + behaves differently for each.
